findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permissions, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> or a domain error type; use map_err to convert io::Error at the boundary

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or missing field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line (missing field or non-numeric value) crashes the program instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ...) in a Result chain; return a domain ParseError with contextual field info

findings.problem: lossy `as u16` cast truncates u32 values silently (e.g. 70000u32 becomes 4464u16)
findings.failure_mode: values outside u16::MAX range wrap silently, corrupting domain data without error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32)? or check range with `if val > u16::MAX { return Err(...) }` before casting

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a Vec for every line when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line; split also produces more parts than needed, increasing GC pressure
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to split into exactly two parts, then .map(|p| p.trim()) on each side; use .get() for indexed access

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into Vec produced by split/collect
findings.failure_mode: empty line or line with fewer than 2 commas causes IndexOutOfBounds panic
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and handle None case; use .get(0) and .get(1) with Option binding

findings.problem: parts[1] unchecked indexing into Vec produced by split/collect
findings.failure_mode: line with only one comma or fewer fields causes IndexOutOfBounds panic
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and handle None; use .get(1) with Option binding

findings.problem: println!() call inside load_sessions mixes I/O (stdout) into data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: hidden side effect in a function that should be pure data loading; breaks testability and composability; logging leaks into the core
findings.fix: remove println! from load_sessions; return parsed records from a pure function; move any logging to the shell layer that calls load_sessions

findings.problem: load_sessions performs I/O (fs::read_to_string) directly; no separation between shell and core
findings.failure_mode: cannot test parsing logic in isolation; I/O coupling prevents pure unit tests of the record-parsing behavior
findings.fix: split into (a) shell function that reads the file and returns String/Result<String>, and (b) pure core function parse_records(&str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: Record fields are pub, allowing external mutation and construction with invalid values
findings.failure_mode: callers can create Record with empty name or out-of-range value, bypassing all validation
findings.fix: make fields private; provide a constructor Record::new(name: String, value: u16) -> Result<Record, InvalidRecordError> or use type-level guards

findings.problem: no try_reserve or bounded allocation strategy for the output Vec
findings.failure_mode: unbounded growth from large files without capacity planning; repeated reallocations
findings.fix: use try_reserve on the Vec with a line-count estimate, or return Result and handle AllocationError

findings.problem: .map(|part| part.trim().to_string()) allocates a String per field unnecessarily
findings.failure_mode: extra heap allocation per field; all allocations are lost after Record construction
findings.fix: use &str directly in Record (name: &str with lifetime) or use Cow<str>; at minimum avoid .to_string() before assigning into String field

findings.problem: no benchmark exists to measure parse-throughput or allocation characteristics
findings.failure_mode: performance claims about this function are unsubstantiated; cannot validate allocation or speed properties
findings.fix: add criterion or custom benchmark measuring parse_records throughput and allocation count

findings.problem: no profiler data (perf, flamegraph, or similar) to identify hot paths in parsing
findings.failure_mode: optimization efforts may target wrong code; allocation hotspots undetected
findings.fix: run perf record/flamegraph or cargo flamegraph on representative workload

findings.problem: no evidence that cargo fmt, cargo test, or cargo clippy were run on this crate
findings.failure_mode: formatting, lint, and test gates unverified; code may have issues not caught by tooling
findings.fix: run cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo test; capture and attach command output

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. 8 BLOCKER findings across forbidden constructs (unwrap, as, unchecked indexing), functional core violation (println! + I/O in core), and missing type safety. The code is non-deliverable in Holzman Rust until all unwrap/as/unchecked-index are replaced with typed error handling, I/O is separated from pure logic, and Record fields are made unrepresentable for illegal states.
